1	# Task 9: procedural robot with idle animation under dramatic lighting
2	
3	Build a scene with Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A robot character built procedurally from primitives (no model files): head, torso, two arms and two legs, with at least five articulated joints (for example neck, shoulders, elbows, hips).
7	2. An idle animation driven from code: it breathes and shifts its weight, and its head and arms move gently. Frames must differ over time.
8	3. Dramatic lighting: a strong key light, a visible coloured rim light, and a dark background, with shadows on a floor.
9	4. The camera frames the whole robot, centred.
10	
11	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
12	
13	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
14	
15	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
16	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
17	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
18	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
19	- When you are done, call `finish`.
20

# Aura3D error and warning codes

Single source for the `explain_error` tool of `@aura3d/mcp` (and for any other agent-loop table). One row per code: `| code | kind | cause | fix |`. Keep each cell on one line; keep the codes verbatim as they appear in console output, `error.code`, `error.name` or `app.diagnostics()`.

| Code | Kind | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RENDERER_MOUNT_FAILED | error (console, `app.diagnostics().errors`) | The production renderer threw while mounting (device lost, a Git LFS pointer file served in place of a GLB/HDR, a missing or hashless asset, a failed pass setup). Nothing draws; the page can still look healthy and non-strict `ready()` can resolve. | Await `app.ready()`, read `app.diagnostics().errors`, pass `strict: true` so `ready()` rejects, check every GLB/HDR is real bytes (not a ~130-byte `version https://git-lfs` stub), keep a fallback, and capture a real frame before calling it done. |
| CONTACT_SHADOW_DEGRADED | warning (console, once) | The contact shadow mask cannot run on this device or frame (missing sampleable depth or a pass setup problem). The mask is skipped; the scene still draws. | No code change is required for a correct frame. input.summary: I wrote src/main.ts with a procedural robot built from capsules, boxes, spheres and cylinders. It has 11 articulated joints: neck/head, chest, hips, two shoulders, two elbows, two hips and two knees. An onFrame idle animation drives breathing, weight shift, and head and arm motion, so frames change over time. The scene has a bright shadow-casting key light, magenta and blue rim lights, a #05060a background and a floor that receives shadows. The perspective camera is centred on the robot at x=0. The typecheck passed. I did not run `vite build` or open the page in a browser, so the rendering is unchecked. The code sets `window.__EVAL_READY__` after `app.ready()` resolves and two animation frames have run.
